items.editor_note: Research on the serving cost of looped transformers: per-recurrence KV-caches and a sharing scheme to shrink them.

items.title: Closing the AI guidance gap in education
items.summary_1line: New ThinkYoung research and lessons from OpenAI’s EMEA education partnerships on supporting teachers, AI literacy, and independent learning.
items.editor_note: Education-policy post from OpenAI; the newest item, but no technical continuation of the papers.

editorial.tldr: This is not one developing story: three unrelated items share only the phrase "closing the gap" in their titles. Two October arXiv papers target model-side gaps, KV-cache memory in looped transformers and the CLIP-style modality gap in embeddings.
editorial.whats_new: OpenAI published ThinkYoung research and EMEA education-partnership lessons on AI literacy for teachers, an education-policy piece with no technical link to the earlier papers.
editorial.why_it_matters: Only the KV-sharing paper bears on inference cost: looped architectures multiply KV-cache memory per recurrence, which sets serving footprint if they reach production.
editorial.take_for_builders: Nothing to change: treat these as three separate reads, and keep the KV-sharing paper on file only if you evaluate looped or recurrent-depth models for serving.

beats.headline: BeNice! proposes KV-sharing to cut looped-model cache memory
beats.summary: Looped architectures reuse layers but create a separate KV-cache per recurrence; the paper shares caches across loops.

beats.summary: A separate research thread on aligning CLIP/CLAP-style multimodal embedding spaces.

beats.headline: OpenAI on the AI guidance gap in education

open_questions: Does BeNice!'s KV-sharing hold quality at the recurrence depths looped models need to match deeper dense models?
Does any serving stack (vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM) add support for looped-architecture KV-sharing?
Does reducing the modality gap measurably improve cross-modal retrieval recall in production embedding pipelines?
